artists.biography:
Steven John Wilson (born 3 November 1967) is an English musician, best known as the founder, lead guitarist, singer and songwriter of progressive rock band Porcupine Tree. He is involved in many other bands and musical projects both as musician and producer (including No-Man and Blackfield) and also maintains a solo career.
Wilson is a self-taught producer, audio engineer, guitar and keyboard player, playing other instruments as and where required (including bass guitar, concert harp, hammered dulcimer and flute).
He used to split his living time between Tel Aviv and London, England, but he no longer holds a permanent residence in Tel Aviv.

perplexity.description:
Intrigue: Progressive Sounds In UK Alternative Music 1979-89 is a curated compilation assembled by Steven Wilson and released by Demon Records in 2023. The collection comprises 58 tracks spanning a decade of British alternative music, featuring artists including Wire, XTC, The Stranglers, Ultravox, Cocteau Twins, Kate Bush, Tears For Fears, The Cure, and New Order. Wilson's curation challenges the prevailing narrative that progressive and conceptual ambition disappeared from rock music after the late 1970s, instead demonstrating that "ambitious, weird and thrilling music was all around you in the '80s—if you looked in the right places."

The compilation explores the experimental and progressive spirit of British alternative music during a period often dismissed by critics. Rather than a retrospective of established hits, Wilson's selection emphasizes lesser-known tracks and deep cuts that showcase the era's creative diversity, spanning electronic experimentation, post-punk innovation, and art rock sophistication. The project functions as both a historical document and a personal statement about Wilson's artistic influences and his conviction that the 1980s deserved reconsideration as a period of genuine musical ambition.

The release was made available in multiple formats to suit different audiences: a comprehensive 4-CD edition housed in a mediabook with an 80-page booklet, a deluxe 7LP vinyl box set pressed at 140 grams and housed in a rigid slipcase, and an edited 2LP vinyl version featuring 19 highlights. All editions include extensive liner notes by James Nice and an introduction by Wilson himself, reflecting the project's emphasis on contextualizing the music within its historical moment.
